Q: Passing file with feature + line number in cucumber.features with Cucumber 7 A:

You are using a rerun file to run you features. As per Cucumber JUnit Platform Engine - Rerunning Failed Scenarios - Using a Rerun file features from a rerun file can be selected for execution:

@Suite
@IncludeEngines("cucumber")
@SelectFile("target/rerun.txt") // Selects the rerun file, must end with .txt 
public class RerunRunCucumber {
}

Note: This requires Cucumber 7.28.0+, so you'll have to upgrade. And if you are indeed re-running feature files please read the whole documentation. There are a few more caveats.

Alternatively, if you are interested in selecting scenarios to run from the CLI you would provide the cucumber.features with a comma separated list of feature files and lines. For example:

mvn test -Dsurefire.includeJUnit5Engines=cucumber -Dcucumber.plugin=pretty -Dcucumber.features=path/to/example.feature:10,path/to/example.feature:16

Alternatively, if you want to select a specific feature programmatically you would use JUnits selectors.

If the feature is on the classpath:

@SelectClasspathResource(value = "com/compangy/example.feature", line = 16)

If the feature is not on the classpath:

@SelectFile(value = "path/to/example.feature", line = 16)

Q: ReactJS Error: react/jsx-no-undef by react-bootstrap A:

Root Cause

Both errors:

  • react/jsx-no-undef
  • 'mountNode' is not defined no-undef

are ESLint scope errors, not React-Bootstrap bugs.

They happen because:

  • JSX components were never imported
  • mountNode was never assigned to a DOM element Once both are defined in scope, the errors go away.

Fixes

First one

react/jsx-no-undef

Import the components you actually use

import React from "react";
import ReactDOM from "react-dom";
import {
  Navbar,
  Nav,
  NavItem,
  NavDropdown,
  MenuItem
} from "react-bootstrap";

Second one

'mountNode' is not defined no-undef

Replace this:

ReactDOM.render(navbarInstance, mountNode);

with this

const mountNode = document.getElementById("root");
ReactDOM.render(navbarInstance, mountNode);
